name: Dimmer Switch 240V

steps.text: Turn off the circuit breakers or remove the fuses feeding the wall box.
Use a voltage meter to make sure the power is off.
Remove the wall plate, unscrew the switch you are replacing and gently pull it out.
Disconnect the wires from the switch.
Turn the breakers back on.
Use a voltage meter to identify the line and load wires that were connected to the switch, and identify the neutral and ground wires.
Turn the breakers back off.
Connect the bare switch wire to ground, white to neutral, red to load and black to line (100 to 277VAC). Make sure the connections are firm with no exposed wire.
With the LED bar on the left, gently place the switch into the wall box and screw it into place.
Turn the breakers back on.
steps.expect: The LED bar and the connected light turn on.

steps.text: Tap the paddle to turn the light on and off to check that the switch works.
Reinstall the wall plate.

notes: In a multi-gang box the dimmer is derated by 200W for each immediately adjacent dimmer.

In 3-way and 4-way circuits every switch must be replaced by an Insteon switch or keypad. Wire one switch to line, neutral and load and the others to line and neutral, using one traveler to share line between boxes and capping the unused traveler and the red wire on switches without the load. Then add the switches to a scene as controllers and responders of each other.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps, about 3 seconds.

notes: As a controller: after the switch beeps, set the responder to the state the scene should recall and press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps or its LED or load flashes. The switch double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.
As a responder: press and hold the scene controller button until it beeps, tap the switch on, then press and hold the switch's SET button until it double-beeps.
Scene mode times out after 4 minutes of inactivity. To leave it, tap the top or bottom of the paddle.
If either LED keeps blinking, the addition failed; tap that device's SET button until the LED stops blinking and try again.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps, about 3 seconds.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller, so the Hub receives the device's reports.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, adjust it to the desired scene state, then press and hold its SET button until it beeps or its LED flashes.
After adding all responders, tap the SET button.
Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until the switch beeps again.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps or its LED blinks.
steps.expect: The switch double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.

notes: To remove the switch as a responder: press and hold the controller's scene button until it beeps, press and hold it again until it beeps, tap the switch on, then press and hold the switch's SET button until it double-beeps.

To remove several responders at once: hold the SET button until it beeps, hold it again until it beeps, then tap it; on each responder tap the scene button and hold its SET button until it beeps or its LED flashes; tap the switch's SET button to finish.

steps.text: Pull the SET button out to create an air gap.
Wait 10 seconds.
Press the SET button in as far as you can and hold it.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: After a couple of seconds the switch double-beeps, the LEDs return to normal brightness and the load turns on.

steps.text: Remove the switch's scene memberships from all of its controllers.
Remove the switch's scene memberships from all of its responders.
Remove the switch from use.

notes: Otherwise controllers retry commands repeatedly, creating network delays.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder, for group 0.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Returns its load and LEDs to their states before a power outage.
